Maya R: Heads up — started bring-up for rainbow-spectrum-v1 embeddings in staging, seeing a weird short-query recall drop and some cluster jitter. posting quick numbers + notes. pls triage when you have a sec :eyes:

Maya R: TL;DR metrics (staging, 10k holdout, cosine):
- baseline albatross-v2 recall@10: 0.78
- rainbow-spectrum-v1 fp32 recall@10: 0.76 (ok)
- rainbow-spectrum-v1 int8 recall@10: 0.62 (drop -0.14)
- silhouette (k=10): baseline 0.41 -> rainbow fp32 0.39 -> int8 0.28

Maya R: repro steps I used:
```
# generate embeddings and run recall eval
embedctl eval --model rainbow-spectrum-v1 --dataset shorttail-10k --dim 1024 --batch 256 --quant none
embedctl eval --model rainbow-spectrum-v1 --dataset shorttail-10k --dim 1024 --batch 256 --quant int8-perchannel
```

Chris P: thanks — did you normalize to unit length before saving the index? we had one model where a missing L2 norm caused short queries to blow up.

Maya R: yep normalized, same pipeline as albatross. code path: `emb_utils.normalize(emb, axis=1)` ran. index build used `hnsw` with ef=128.

Sanjeev K: pinging the quant tests I ran: I tried both per-channel and symmetric int8. per-channel gave slightly better recall but still down. quick logs:
```
quantize --input model.fp32 --output model.int8 --method per-channel --clamp 6.0
eval --emb-file model.int8.embeddings --k 10 --metric recall
# output: recall@10 0.62, recall@1 0.31
```

Sanjeev K: also experimented with disabling whitening/spectral-scaling step — that changed cluster shapes. Looks like quantization interacts badly with our spectral-whitening preproc.

Lee W: interesting. can you dump top-10 neighbors for a few failing short queries (fp32 vs int8)? small diff in neighbor ordering could indicate quantization noise in high-dim subspace.

Maya R: posted example for query id 3245:
- fp32 top3 ids: [1201, 45, 87] (cosine: [0.89, 0.87, 0.86])
- int8 top3 ids: [45, 1201, 4002] (cosine approx: [0.84, 0.83, 0.82])
notes: a healthy swap but also a new unrelated id introduced at rank 3 which seems to push true positive out of top10 for some queries.

Chris P: maybe check per-dimension dynamic range — if a few dims dominate, quantization may clip them. can you run `embed-stats --model ... --histogram` and paste top dims.

Maya R: ran hist dump, top 5 dims (abs mean) are ~2-3x next decile. attaching snippet: `dim_peak_idxs: [12, 78, 901]`

Sanjeev K: suggestion: try scale-clip with per-dim calibration (clamp to 3 sigma) before quantize, or run minmax per-channel symmetric quant rather than global. I can spin a quick bake.

eval-bot: automated-eval finished for rainbow-spectrum-v1 int8-perchannel — regression detected vs baseline albatross-v2: recall@10 delta -0.16 (p<0.01). ticket created: #ML-7832

Lee W: also please sanity-check batch size when generating embeddings. fp32 used batch 256, int8 precompute path used batch 64 in my earlier run and we saw micro-drift. inconsistent micro-batching can change KVs ordering if there's nondeterminism.

Maya R: good catch — I re-ran int8 with batch 256, same drop though.

Chris P: next actionable list: 
1) Sanjeev to try per-dim clamp + symmetric int8 bake (quick).
2) Maya to collect 50 failing short queries + neighbor diffs and put in a shared gist.
3) Lee to run silhouette + visual UMAP for fp32 vs int8 to see cluster bleed.
4) If we confirm quantization is root, maybe enable selective fp16 for top-k dims or fallback to fp32 for short queries.

Maya R: I'll open a canary gating PR to block int8 rollout until we have mitigation. adding tags: @chris @sanjeev @lee :thumbsup: 

Sanjeev K: starting a quick bake now, will post results in ~20m.

Lee W: adding note — remind infra to pin kernel `cuBLAS 12.1` vs 12.0 differences caused tiny float-delta in a past case. environment parity matters.

Chris P: thanks team. if no objections I'll convert this to a short postmortem if we need to rollback a canary later.

Maya R: no objections. will update thread with gist link and the PR. :rocket:
